# Where

> A self-hosted web app that remembers which cupboard, shelf, box or tray each
> thing in your home is in. Photograph an item, type its name, and a vision
> model running on your own server writes the detail that tells it apart from
> the near-identical ones. Free and open source under the GPL version 3.
> Currently in beta.

Where is made by Lightmorphic Ltd (Mildenhall, England) and given away. There
is no hosted version, no account and no paid tier. You run it yourself with
Docker on your own machine.

## What it does

- **Places**: a flat list of names, such as "Cupboard 1", "Top shelf",
  "Storage box", "Tray 14". No nesting and no hierarchy.
- **Items**: each belongs to exactly one place and holds a photograph, a name,
  a description, a free-text note, and a "gone" flag for things used up or
  thrown out.
- **Automatic descriptions**: the photograph is sent to Ollama running on the
  same server, and the model writes the distinguishing detail, for example
  "black, right-angle plug, about a metre". Generation never blocks saving; if
  the model is unreachable the item still saves. Any description can be edited
  and a hand edit is never overwritten.
- **Bulk add from one photograph**: photograph a whole tray, the model returns
  a list of the objects it can see, and the user ticks, corrects and saves them
  all into that place at once.
- **QR labels**: one per place, laid out for 30 x 20 mm thermal label rolls.
  Scanning a label opens that place. Several places can be printed as one sheet.
- **Search**: across item name, description and note. Results read
  "USB-C cable — Tray 14".
- **Phone first**: installable to the home screen as a progressive web app,
  with camera capture and in-browser QR scanning. Camera access requires https.
- **Accounts**: everyone signs in with their own name and password and shares
  one list of places and items. The first account created administers the copy.
  Self-service sign-up is off by default.

## What it deliberately does not do

No prices, purchase dates, suppliers, receipts, warranties, quantities,
categories, tags, nested locations, lending records or barcode lookup against
retail databases. It is not an inventory or insurance system. Accounts exist so
a household can share one list, not so each person can keep a separate one.

## Privacy

Nothing leaves the user's server. The vision model runs locally through Ollama.
No cloud AI provider is involved and there is no API key to supply. The website
sets no cookies and carries no analytics. The app sets one cookie, which keeps
you signed in on your own server.

## Running it

Docker, two containers (the app and Ollama), one bind-mounted folder holding a
SQLite database, the photographs and the session key. There is no `.env` file
and no configuration in the compose file beyond the published port and that
folder: the model, its address, the timeout, the address printed into QR labels
and whether strangers may sign up are all on the Settings page inside the app.
The default model is `moondream`, about 1.7 GB, which runs on a small machine
with no graphics card; `minicpm-v` does the bulk tray listing better if there is
memory for it.

## Built with

Python, Flask, SQLite, Pillow, qrcode and waitress. Plain CSS, no framework and
no build step.
